government.name: Shogunate
government.description: The bakufu is a military government held in the Shōgun's hand, ruling the realm on behalf of an Imperial court that has long since stopped ruling itself. Land is held by samurai houses at the Shōgun's pleasure: confiscation and reassignment of a clan's fiefs is the bakufu's most-used political tool. Beneath the Shōgun stand the shugo and the great daimyō houses; beneath them, the karō and the lesser samurai; beneath them, the soldiery and the peasants under arms.
government.effects: - Settlement security +1{newline}- Settlement cultural weight +30%{newline}- Settlement mercantilism +25%{newline}- Vassal fiefs reassignable at low influence cost

government.name: Daimyō Realm
government.description: A daimyō rules his han as a sovereign within his own borders, owing only formal loyalty to the Shōgun in distant Kyōto. The clan's senior retainers — the karō — hold the inner council; the lesser samurai hold the outer fiefs; ji-samurai and ashigaru fill the host. Where the daimyō rides personally, the laws of the han are whatever he says they are; where he does not, the karō rule in his name.
government.effects: - Petitioning rights yield no relation loss{newline}- Settlement stability +5%{newline}- Settlement draft efficiency +15%{newline}- Settlement mercantilism +20%

government.name: Ikkō League
government.description: The Ikkō-Ikki are not a kingdom but a confederation — autonomous leagues (kō) of Shin Buddhist farmers, ji-samurai, town merchants and ikkō priests, recognising the Monshu of Honganji as their spiritual head and convening in great assemblies to decide war, peace and the price of rice. There are no hereditary daimyō here. There is the kō; there is the Monshu; there is the Nembutsu; and there is the wall of Honganji.
government.effects: - Settlement militia +2{newline}- Settlement loyalty +1 (Shin faith){newline}- Settlement mercantilism +35%{newline}- Reduced influence cost for league-wide decisions
